_comment: Structural contract for a delivered literature-deep-review report.
This file is the TARGET the report is measured against. It is deliberately
independent of what any individual run happened to produce: a gate that
reads its expectation out of the run's own output can never detect a
shortfall. Edit thresholds here, not in the checker.
The Markdown is a DELIVERABLE, not a draft of the PDF. Only the PDF was
ever measured against required_sections, so review.md shipped for months
with no Introduction, Methods, Conclusions or Next steps at all — the two
deliverables were structurally different documents built from the same
model, which is precisely what the model exists to prevent.
build_review.py refuses to write a file that is missing any of them.
A Results section that lists quotes is a quote catalogue. For each central
claim the report must separate the observed result (anchored by the
verbatim quote) from the authors' interpretation, from the reviewer's own
inference, from the contradiction or alternative explanation, from the
evidence gap. Those five facets are the difference between a scientific
document and a search result.
statement_rule: every narrative statement must EITHER cite evidence_ids
that exist in evidence/evidence.jsonl, OR set "inference": true and be
rendered under inference_label. A statement with neither is unattributable
and both builders abort. inference_label is read by BOTH renderers, so the
label cannot be changed here and left stale in one of the two outputs.
central_claims: 'grounded' (every claim carrying a qualifying supporting or
contradicting quote, per support_policy) or 'all'.
require_artifact: claim_narratives.jsonl USED to be optional, and that is
how two broad runs of this skill produced structurally different reports —
one separated all 14 claims into the five facets, the other authored none
and shipped a bare quote catalogue. Silence is not evidence a narrative was
unwanted; for the required modes it is a missing deliverable. Set false to
opt out deliberately.
A target-evidence review must have looked for disconfirming evidence. One
shipped review carried a safety_contradictions axis and a deliberate
contradiction search; another, same skill and same mode, had six axes that
were all mechanism or efficacy and NOT ONE covering harm, null results or
risk — on a target whose central development risk is exactly that, and
whose own Next steps asked for a safety adjudication. A review that
searched only for confirmation cannot report that it found none.
Satisfied by an axis whose name mentions safety / contradiction / risk /
null / limitation / counter / adverse, OR by any contradicting quote
anywhere: the requirement is that the review looked, not that it named an
axis a particular way.
The report opens with a 3-panel Phylo infographic — A, B, C left to right,
Signifier headings, DieGrotesk body text, the Phylo palette — adapted from
target-prioritization-dashboard/skills/target-infographic. See
references/infographic_prompt_template.txt.
TWO PROFILES. 'target' keeps that skill's biology -> disease mechanism ->
therapeutic rationale arc. 'general' covers every other review this skill
runs (mechanism, biomarker, modality comparison, direction-of-effect):
A = the system, B = what the evidence shows, C = what follows. Same shape,
same styling, different semantics. scripts/infographic_spec.py picks the
profile from the question and the author may override it.
generation_tool: the active Biomni agent must load and call GenerateImage
with the exact persisted request. A pseudo-call in prose or a placeholder
PNG does not satisfy the contract. The request and receipt hashes bind the
current evidence-backed prompt to the installed image.
require_media_output_check: Biomni Read must visually check the returned
image for Phylo styling, legibility, clipping, and garbled labels before
the image is installed and the report is built.
require_verified_spec: the spec is SEEDED from the report model and then
VERIFIED — every number, identifier and citation in it must appear in an
accepted evidence row. An infographic is the first thing a reader sees and
would otherwise be the one part of the document nobody could audit, sitting
on page one above everything that is checked.
caption_marker was 'visual abstract'; both are accepted by the gates so a
run built before the infographic existed still passes.

synthesis_table._comment: One row per evidence axis (claim cluster) with bottom line + strongest support tier. This is the reader's map of the whole review.

synthesis_chart._comment: Grounded claims by axis and support tier. Drawn by the review, never presented as a paper figure. Counts MUST be recomputed from claim_evidence_matrix.csv at build time, never hand-entered.

_comment: min_by_mode is the conservative fallback only. The user's fixed or
resolved adaptive run minimum overrides it. An unresolved adaptive
minimum must fail before report assembly rather than fall back silently.
min_fraction_of_croppable is zero by default so corpus size cannot silently
raise the user's chosen minimum. A nonzero custom contract still counts
coverage by distinct paper IDs, not several crops from one paper.
selection governs WHICH figures are shown, per scripts/figure_selection.
A figure used to reach the report only by having its caption quoted, so
figure choice was a side effect of quote-type choice: 45 verbatim anchors
became 6 figures, one paper contributed 3 figures to a single claim, and a
review's therapeutic-strategies schematic was embedded under a claim about
lipid metabolism. Figures are now scored against the claim text and drawn
from the papers that claim already cites.
These are caps on crowding. Beyond the user-selected minimum, include a
figure only when it adds material, nonredundant panel-level information.
By default one paper contributes at most one figure to one claim; a
second figure for that claim should come from a different cited paper.
The minimum is a floor, not a stopping point. Selection additionally
checks decision-critical axes explicitly marked figure_priority=true and
adds one materially relevant visual to an otherwise uncovered priority
axis when eligible supply exists. It does not force decorative visuals
onto background axes or impose a fixed coverage fraction.
min_relevance and min_shared_terms are calibrated together on real
figure/claim pairs from the shipped reports (see
tests/test_figure_selection.py::SHIPPED_PAIRS). Neither works alone: the
score cannot reject 'Figure 2 Brain sections.' against a claim mentioning
the brain, which scores above three genuine matches, and the shared-term
count cannot rank. Change one and re-check the separation.
allow_review_figures false excludes figures from review articles, whose
figures are drawn rather than measured and so cannot be primary evidence.
allow_context_figures is false by default: source models and review
diagrams do not satisfy the source-figure floor. A custom contract may
permit them as explicitly illustrative-only context; they never change
a claim's evidence-derived support tier.
These values are mirrored in figure_selection.DEFAULT_POLICY and a test
asserts they agree. The contract wins at runtime, so a drift is invisible
in a real run and only changes behaviour under direct use of the defaults.
PROVENANCE. Each embedded figure carries boxes over the in-figure text
matching its claim's own terms, and its caption names both signals: the
caption terms that scored and the boxed regions (scripts/figure_provenance).
Two reports shipped 27 figures with no indication of why any of them was
chosen. When easyocr is absent the caption SAYS the figure was not read
rather than falling silent, because silence reads as 'checked, nothing
found'.
A locator that says 'Unknown' when the block is the Abstract is a defect,
not a gap. Long section values mean a whole heading leaked into the label.
'front matter' is forbidden FOR EVIDENCE ROWS. The parser uses it for
page-1 blocks before the first heading — titles, author lists,
affiliations — and none of those is ever evidence of anything. Ten
abstract sentences shipped located at 'page 1 · Front matter' because the
abstract detector needed a single 200-character block and Nature-family
PDFs split the abstract into shorter ones. scripts/section_labels.py fixes
the cause; this entry is the backstop if it ever regresses.

references._comment: Scraped page-chrome in a title is a data-cleanliness bug; an uncited reference means the list and the body disagree.
